title: Thirty in the Lock-up
subtitle: Thirty young men were picked up after a stone-throwing night; most were just there
coldOpen: 23:40 last night. Stones hit a police post near the square.
01:00. Thirty young men are picked up in a sweep.
By morning, mothers are outside the station.

briefing.grievance: Families say their sons were walking home from a wedding when the sweep happened. Officers say the stone-throwers are among the thirty and will not be separated under pressure.
knownFacts: Thirty people aged 17 to 26 are held; none has been produced before a magistrate yet.
Two officers were injured by stones at 23:40.
The wedding hall emptied at 23:30, two streets from the post.
unverifiedClaims: A post says the thirty are a “gang” from outside the city.
A voice note says the police beat two boys inside.
briefing.responsibility: You oversee the police station and the magistrate’s liaison. The law gives you 24 hours and the families give you less.
briefing.objective: Separate the few who threw stones from the many who did not, lawfully and visibly, before the city decides for you.

decisions.title: Mothers at the station
decisions.situation: Forty women are outside the station asking for names and reasons. Inside, no one has been told what they are held for.

options.title: Read the names and the grounds to the families
options.preview: Each family hears the name, the pickup point and the alleged offence.
options.authority: Duty of candour: say what is known and what is not
options.consequence: The list is public. Families know who is inside and why.

options.title: Let a legal-aid lawyer in to meet each detainee
options.preview: A volunteer lawyer meets all thirty with an officer present.
options.authority: Duty to hear grievances; Article 19(1)(a) free expression
options.consequence: Inside, each boy gives his account. Outside, the mothers are told he has been seen.

options.title: Clear the families from the station gate
options.preview: Officers push the women back to the main road.
options.authority: Article 19(2)–(3): restrictions must be reasonable and specific
options.consequence: Mothers are pushed off the pavement. The story becomes about that.

delayed.message: The crackdown hardens people who had stayed out of it. More arrive, angrier.

options.title: Say nothing until the paperwork is done
options.preview: No names, no grounds; the voice note about beatings spreads.
options.consequence: The silence confirms the worst rumours.

simple.title: Mothers at the station

o-d006-1-disperse.title: Push the families away

o-d006-1-disperse.consequence: Now the story is about mothers being pushed.

o-d006-1-wait.title: Say nothing yet

o-d006-1-wait.consequence: The silence makes the rumours stronger.

decisions.title: Who threw the stones?
decisions.situation: The post camera shows five figures. The guest list covers twenty-two of the thirty. The footage deletes itself in three days.

options.title: Preserve the footage and match it, name by name
options.preview: Officers copy the clip and compare it with the thirty, with the lawyer watching.
options.authority: Due process: establish the facts before acting on them
options.consequence: Five figures, five names to check. Twenty-five have nothing to answer.

options.title: Get every detainee examined by a hospital doctor
options.preview: An independent doctor examines all thirty and records findings.
options.authority: Duty to keep essential services running
options.consequence: The beating rumour meets a medical sheet.

options.title: Charge all thirty with rioting
options.preview: One charge sheet for everyone picked up that night.
options.authority: Due process: a public charge needs verified evidence
options.consequence: Wedding guests are charged with a riot they walked past.

options.title: Let the footage wait
options.preview: Nobody copies the clip; the 72-hour clock runs.
options.consequence: The only way to tell the five from the thirty is ticking away.

simple.title: Who threw the stones?

decisions.title: Twenty-four hours
decisions.situation: The magistrate is available at 3 pm. Officers want all thirty remanded as a group. The lawyer wants twenty-five released now.

options.title: Release all but those matched to the footage
options.preview: Those not on the clip walk out; the matched few go before the magistrate.
options.authority: Article 19(1)(b): peaceful assembly, policed in proportion
options.consequence: Twenty-five walk out. Five face the court with evidence.

options.title: Produce only the matched five, release the rest
options.preview: Five are produced with the footage; twenty-five are released with notices.
options.authority: Proportionality: act against the few causing harm, not the many
options.consequence: The court sees evidence against five, not thirty.

options.title: Seek remand for all thirty
options.preview: The whole group is produced as “rioters” and remand is requested.
options.authority: Articles 21 and 22: liberty and safeguards on arrest
options.consequence: Wedding guests spend a week in jail for the five.

options.title: Miss the 3 pm slot
options.preview: Nobody is produced; the 24-hour limit passes.
options.consequence: The detention is now unlawful for all thirty.

options.title: Hold all thirty for a week

rightsMoments.question: Thirty people were picked up near a stone-throwing. What must happen within 24 hours?

options.text: Each person must be told the grounds, allowed a lawyer, and produced before a magistrate; those without individual grounds released.
options.feedback: Correct. Arrest safeguards apply person by person; a group sweep does not change that.

options.text: The group can be held until the investigation finishes, however long that takes.
options.feedback: Detention beyond 24 hours needs a magistrate’s order, and grounds must be individual.

options.text: They can be held as long as no one is physically harmed.
options.feedback: Liberty is not only about injury; detention itself needs lawful grounds and judicial oversight.

rightsMoments.principle: Article 22 requires that an arrested person be told the grounds, allowed to consult a lawyer, and produced before a magistrate within 24 hours. Article 21 protects liberty from arbitrary detention.
rightsMoments.why: Twenty-five of the thirty were wedding guests; only individual evidence could separate them from the five.

source.label: Constitution of India, Articles 21 and 22 (India Code)

simple.question: Thirty people were picked up near a stone fight. What must happen within 24 hours?

options.a: Each must be told why, get a lawyer, and see a judge. Free those with no proof.
options.b: Hold the group until the case is finished.
options.c: Hold them as long as nobody is hurt.

feedback.a: Yes! Rights work person by person.
feedback.b: No. After 24 hours a judge must decide, person by person.
feedback.c: Being locked up is itself a harm. It needs real reasons.

simple.principle: Anyone arrested must be told why, may see a lawyer, and must see a judge within 24 hours.
simple.why: Most of the thirty were wedding guests. Only real proof could tell them apart from the five.

improvements.text: Preserve the one piece of evidence that separates the few from the many.
improvements.simple: Save the clip that tells the few from the many.

improvements.text: Use the 24 hours to release, not to build a group charge.
improvements.simple: Use the 24 hours to free the innocent.

improvements.text: Tell families the grounds early; silence writes the rumour for you.

closing.good: Twenty-five went home with their mothers, five went before a magistrate with evidence, and the officers got a case worth having.
closing.mixed: Most went home, but late, and the city is not sure the five will ever be named.
closing.poor: Thirty were held for the sins of five, and the five are still out there.
